papers.title: Yinchenhao Decoction Protects Against Severe Acute Pancreatitis-Associated Liver Injury Through Suppression of Hepatic TLR4/NF-?B/NLRP3 Signalling.
papers.authors: Wu X, Yao J, Meng J, He X, Hu Q, Yang Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Liver injury is a major complication of severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) and is associated with poor clinical outcomes, yet effective pharmacological interventions remain limited. Yinchenhao decoction (YCHD), a classical traditional Chinese medicine formula, has shown anti-inflammatory and organ-protective properties. However, its role and underlying mechanism in SAP-associated liver injury remain unclear.
SAP was induced in mice by retrograde infusion of 2% sodium taurocholate into the biliopancreatic duct. Pancreatic, hepatic, and serum samples were collected 24 h after SAP induction and treatment. Histopathological injury and serum biochemical indices were assessed. The hepatic expression of TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 pathway-related molecules was evaluated by qPCR and western blotting. The hepatic distribution of major YCHD-derived compounds was characterized by HPLC-MS/MS.
YCHD markedly reduced serum amylase, alanine aminotransferase, and aspartate aminotransferase levels, and alleviated histopathological injury in both pancreatic and hepatic tissues. Mechanistically, YCHD suppressed the hepatic mRNA expression of TLR4, NF-κB, NLRP3, and ASC, and reduced the protein levels of key inflammatory mediators associated with TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 signalling. HPLC-MS/MS analysis identified multiple YCHD-derived compounds in liver tissue, among which geniposide showed the highest hepatic abundance.
YCHD protects against SAP-associated liver injury, at least in part, through suppression of the hepatic TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammatory axis. The prominent hepatic accumulation of geniposide suggests that it may represent one of the principal bioactive constituents contributing to the therapeutic effects of YCHD.

papers.title: Nodose ganglion vagal afferents promote electroacupuncture efficacy in the gut-brain axis via proteasome restoration and CXCL10 suppression.
papers.authors: Li J, Yang J, Wang J, Xie G, Zheng Z, Huang Y et al.
papers.abstract: Electroacupuncture is a potent neuromodulatory strategy for mitigating intestinal pathologies. Nevertheless, the role of primary visceral sensory apparatuses in transducing somatosensory acupuncture signals remains unclear. Here, we sought to delineate the neuroanatomical necessity and cell type-specific molecular reprogramming within the nodose ganglion, the primary sensory relay of vagal afferents, underlying electroacupuncture-mediated intestinal homeostasis. Retrograde tracing confirmed a direct neuroanatomical conduit between the distal colon and nodose ganglion sensory neurons. Under pathological conditions, the nodose ganglion dynamically sensed colonic inflammation, manifesting as profound transcriptomic shifts. Electroacupuncture at Zusanli (ST36) significantly attenuated UC severity, suppressed systemic inflammation, and restored both physical (zonula occludens-1 and claudin-1) and chemical (Muc2 and Tff3) mucosal barriers. Crucially, targeted ablation of nodose ganglion vagal afferents completely abolished these macroscopic and molecular protective effects, along with the blockade of electroacupuncture-evoked cervical vagal discharge and colonic motility reflexes. Multomic deconvolution revealed that colitis triggered severe proteasome dysregulation and aberrant Cxcl10-mediated satellite glia/macrophage-to-neuron crosstalk within the nodose ganglion. Remarkably, electroacupuncture precisely reversed this pathological reprogramming by upregulating the expression of core proteasome-associated hub genes (Psma2, Psmd14, and Eif2s1) and potently quenching Cxcl10-induced neuroimmune hypersensitivity. These findings suggest that vagal sensory afferents within the nodose ganglion function as indispensable anatomical bottlenecks and functional responders for electroacupuncture-mediated colitis remission. By expanding the classic "acupoint-organ-center" paradigm, these findings demonstrate that disease-state sensory ganglia actively gate neuromodulatory therapy, providing a high-resolution molecular foundation for the clinical translation of electroacupuncture in treating intestinal disease.

papers.title: Maoyu Extract Suppresses Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Progression via PI3K/AKT Signaling Blockade: An Integrated Network Pharmacology and Experimental Validation Study.
papers.authors: Song M, Tan J, Liu L, Zhang Y, Wang B, Zhai Y
papers.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a leading cause of global cancer mortality. Maoyu extract (MY) is a traditional Chinese medicine formulation comprising Ranunculus ternatus Thunb. and Houttuynia cordata Thunb., used traditionally to treat inflammatory lung ailments and nodules. This study aims to systematically investigate the anti-NSCLC efficacy of Maoyu extract and elucidate its underlying molecular mechanisms, specifically focusing on the PI3K/AKT signaling axis. Active compounds and targets were screened using the TCMSP database and validated via molecular docking. Predicted mechanisms were verified in vitro using A549 and NCI-H1299 cell lines and in vivo using a syngeneic Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) mouse model. Network analysis identified 15 active compounds (including β-sitosterol, kaempferol, and quercetin) and 197 targets. MY significantly inhibited cell proliferation, induced apoptosis, and blocked the PI3K/AKT axis. In the LLC model, MY reduced tumor volume by 56.77%, matching cisplatin's efficacy without inducing significant body weight loss. Maoyu extract exerts potent anti-NSCLC effects by suppressing proliferation and inducing apoptosis through the targeted blockade of the PI3K/AKT signaling axis, providing a scientific basis for its traditional use.

papers.title: Altered centrality and connectivity in motor networks following Xingnao Kaiqiao acupuncture for acute ischemic stroke: a randomized controlled, exploratory fMRI study.
papers.authors: Xie Y, Guo X, Qi J, Zhang K, Ying W, He Y et al.
papers.abstract: Xingnao Kaiqiao (XNKQ) acupuncture is recommended as an adjunctive intervention for motor dysfunction after acute ischemic stroke (AIS), yet its neuroplastic mechanisms remain unclear. In this randomized, exploratory study, 28 AIS patients were randomly assigned to XNKQ acupuncture plus medication (n = 14) or medication-only (n = 14) to receive 10 sessions of treatment over 14 days. Clinical assessments and resting-state fMRI scanning were conducted before and after the intervention, with brain reorganization analyzed using voxel-wise degree centrality (DC) and seed-based functional connectivity (FC). We found that better recovery in the XNKQ group, reflected by more improvements in NIHSS, total and upper-extremity FMA scores, was correlated with reduced DC in the ipsilesional primary motor cortex (iM1) concurrent with attenuated FC to the contralesional supplementary motor area (cSMA), alongside increased DC in the bilateral SMA and preserved FC between SMA and cerebellar regions. Further exploratory mediation analysis suggested that change in iM1-cSMA FC potentially mediated the relationship between iM1 DC normalization and motor recovery. These preliminary findings suggest that XNKQ acupuncture may facilitate early motor recovery after AIS through normalization of ipsilesional M1 hub centrality and modulation of M1-SMA cross-hemispheric connectivity, providing candidate network markers for acupuncture-associated neuroplasticity.

papers.title: Combating Porcine-Origin Multidrug-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus with a Traditional Chinese Medicine: In Vitro Efficacy and Mechanistic Insights.
papers.authors: He J, Mao X, Mei J, Li H, Wang P, Rasoul LM et al.
papers.abstract: The emergence of multidrug-resistant bacteria poses a significant threat to global public health, highlighting the urgent need for novel, effective, and safe alternative agents to combat these pathogens. This study aimed to evaluate the in vitro antibacterial activity and mechanism of action of Galla chinensis extract (GCE) against porcine-origin Staphylococcus aureus. The bioactive components of Galla chinensis were extracted by water extraction with water-bath heating. The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) was determined using the two-fold broth microdilution method. The in vitro antibacterial activity of the GCE extract against S. aureus was evaluated by the disk diffusion assay and by monitoring bacterial growth curves at various extract concentrations. The antibacterial mechanism was investigated by assessing key indicators of bacterial membrane and envelope integrity following exposure to the extract. The GCE exhibited potent inhibitory activity against S. aureus, with an inhibition zone diameter of 3.60 ± 0.10 cm. The MIC of GCE against S. aureus was 15.63 mg/mL. Compared with the control group, bacterial growth was markedly suppressed in the extract-treated groups in a dose-dependent manner, with the inhibitory effect strengthening as the extract concentration increased. Following treatment, the alkaline phosphatase (AKP) activity, soluble protein concentration, and extracellular nucleic acid leakage of S. aureus increased in a concentration-dependent manner. Galla chinensis exhibits potent in vitro antibacterial activity against S. aureus by inhibiting bacterial growth, and its underlying mechanism is associated with disrupting the cell wall and cell membrane integrity of S. aureus.

papers.title: Global divergence of stroke and major depressive disorder: unveiling a potential "hidden stagnation" pattern through an integrated medicine perspective.
papers.authors: Jia K, Qian LL, Zhao FC, Sun Q, Zhang MM, Li YF
papers.abstract:
Major depressive disorder (MDD) is associated with increased stroke risk and can be conceptualized in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) as emotional constraint or "Qi Stagnation" that may contribute to "Blood Stasis." However, the country-level ecological relationship between stroke burden and MDD prevalence remains unclear, and high-stroke settings may have under-recognized MDD because of differences in data availability, diagnostic practices, mental health services, and cultural symptom expression. This study quantifies this ecological association and interprets it through an Integrated Medicine framework.
Using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 data, we analyzed age-standardized stroke Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) rates for all stroke and age-standardized prevalence rates for the GBD cause category of MDD across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023. An exploratory Diagnostic Gap Score (ZStroke-ZMDD) was developed to identify countries and territories with disproportionate stroke burden relative to reported MDD prevalence.
A negative ecological correlation emerged globally and strengthened over time (r = -0.059 in 1990 versus r = -0.218 in 2023, P = 0.002). The highest stroke burden quartile (Q4) reported lower MDD prevalence (2639.9/100 000) than the lowest quartile (3067.0/100 000; mean difference 427.1/100 000, 95% CI: 121.52 to 732.58), despite an 8.3% increase in stroke burden in Q4. The score identified clusters with disproportionate stroke burden relative to MDD prevalence in Eastern Europe, Southeast Asia, and Pacific Island settings.
Low reported MDD prevalence in high-stroke countries and territories suggests a potential diagnostic, reporting, or data-quality mismatch rather than biological protection. These ecological findings do not prove that undiagnosed MDD causes stroke burden, but they support culturally adapted mental health screening in primary care, stroke-prevention clinics, and community health settings, with referral pathways for those who screen positive.

papers.title: Paclitaxel induces region-specific microglial remodeling associated with chronic behavioral deficits and modulated by electroacupuncture in rats.
papers.authors: Hiraiwa S, Muramoto T, Umeda M, Ebara S, Fukuda F
papers.abstract: Chemotherapy-associated behavioral deficits, including cognitive impairment and depression, collectively termed chemobrain, often persist into the chronic phase after treatment, yet their underlying cellular mechanisms remain unclear. In particular, it remains unknown whether long-lasting behavioral deficits are associated with sustained neuroinflammatory responses or other forms of microglial alteration. We therefore examined whether chronic behavioral deficits were associated with region-specific microglial morphological alterations and inflammatory gene expression changes, and how EA intervention was associated with these alterations. Male SD rats were assigned to the Control, PTX, and PTX + EA groups. Cognitive and emotional behaviors were assessed using behavioral tests. Microglial morphology in the hippocampus across the dorsoventral axis and mPFC was analyzed using skeleton analysis, and inflammatory gene expression was evaluated by qPCR. PTX induced cognitive impairment and depressive-like behavior, accompanied by a selective reduction in microglial process number and length in the dentate gyrus of the dorsal hippocampus and the infralimbic cortex of the mPFC. Microglial morphology differed between the PTX and PTX + EA groups in both regions, although the difference in the dorsal dentate gyrus was limited to process number. No significant changes in the inflammatory genes examined were detected in the hippocampus or mPFC. Thus, PTX produced chronic behavioral deficits accompanied by selective microglial remodeling in the dorsal dentate gyrus and infralimbic cortex, but not in the ventral hippocampus, with no detectable changes in inflammatory gene expression. Behavioral outcomes and microglial morphology differed between the PTX and PTX + EA groups, indicating an association between EA intervention and region-specific microglial remodeling.

papers.title: Shugan Xiaozhi Formula Reduces Hepatic Steatosis and Stiffness in MASLD Patients with Elevated ALT: An Exploratory 24-Week Randomized Trial.
papers.authors: Sun Y, Han Z, Li C, Hu D, Xie F, Li Q et al.
papers.abstract:
Metabolic dysfunction-related fatty liver disease (MASLD) affects approximately one-third of adults worldwide. The most common manifestations in the early stage are liver dysfunction, hepatic steatosis，metabolic abnormalities, and obesity. The failure of single behavioral interventions and the limited availability of treatment drugs remain unmet clinical needs.
In this 24-week, multicenter, prospective, randomized, open-label, active-controlled, proof-of-concept trial conducted in China, 285 participants with MASLD (ALT >40U/L to 5×ULN) were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive Shugan Xiaozhi Formula (SGXZ) granules or vitamin E 300mg/day. The primary exploratory endpoints were changes in hepatic steatosis measured by MRI-proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) and FibroScan-controlled attenuation parameter (CAP), and changes in liver stiffness by transient elastography (TE) and magnetic resonance elastography (MRE). Additional outcomes included liver enzymes, anthropometric measures, and safety parameters. Analyses were performed in the completer population (n=152) using ANCOVA and logistic regression.
At week 24, SGXZ significantly reduced MRI-PDFF (adjusted mean difference vs vitamin E, -3.44 percentage points; 95% CI, -5.18 to -1.69; P<0.001) and CAP (-45.42dB/m; 95% CI, -58.37 to -32.47; P<0.001). A higher proportion of SGXZ recipients achieved a ≥1-category reduction in MRI-PDFF-defined steatosis grade (22.4% vs 5.3%; OR, 5.83; P=0.007) and a ≥30dB/m reduction in CAP (82.9% vs 39.5%; OR, 8.01; P<0.001). Liver stiffness parameters also improved more with SGXZ (TE, -1.14 kPa; P<0.001; MRE, -0.06m/s; P<0.001). Changes in ALT and AST did not differ between groups, whereas GGT normalization was more frequent with SGXZ (52.3% vs 27.7%; OR, 2.87; P=0.010). SGXZ was also associated with significantly greater reductions in body weight (between-group mean difference, -2.69kg; 95% CI, -3.60 to -1.78; P < 0.001), BMI (-0.94kg/m²; 95% CI, -1.26 to -0.62; P < 0.001), and WHR (-0.04; 95% CI, -0.08 to -0.01; P = 0.020). SGXZ was generally well tolerated; gastrointestinal events were more common but were mild and self-limiting. No serious adverse events or clinically meaningful laboratory safety signals occurred.
In this exploratory trial, SGXZ was associated with greater reductions in hepatic steatosis, imaging-based liver stiffness, body weight, BMI, and WHR than vitamin E, with an acceptable safety profile. These findings suggest that SGXZ represents a highly promising compound natural medicine therapeutic option for the complex metabolic diseases MASLD/MASH. It meets the urgent clinical need for safe and effective therapies to comprehensively improve patients' conditions. Of course, these findings require further validation in large-scale trials with sufficient statistical power.
ChiCTR2200057595.

papers.title: Jinfeng Pills Ameliorate Levonorgestrel-Induced Ovarian Injury by Modulating ApoA1-Associated Cholesterol Homeostasis and PI3K/Akt Signaling.
papers.authors: Hu Y, Li G, Ni Q, Zhong R, Zhou J, Guo X et al.
papers.abstract:
Jinfeng Pills (JFP, NMPA approval No. Z20064400) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula clinically used to regulate menstruation and support ovulation. It consists of nine medicinal materials: Epimedium brevicornu Maxim. (Yinyanghuo), Cervus elaphus Linnaeus (Lurong), Panax ginseng C.A.Mey. (Renshen), Equus asinus (EJiao), Ligustrum lucidum W.T.Aiton (Nvzhenzi), Reynoutria multiflora (Thunb.) Moldenke (Heshouwu), Curculigo orchioides Gaertn. (Xianmao), Cinnamomum cassia (L.) J.Presl (Rougui) and Leonurus japonicus Houtt. (Yimucao). Previous studies have demonstrated the protective effects of JFP against ovarian dysfunction. However, the potential protective effects of JFP against ovarian injury induced by chronic exposure to levonorgestrel (LNG), a progestin commonly used in emergency contraception, and their underlying mechanisms remain unclear.
This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of JFP against ovarian injury induced by chronic LNG exposure and to explore the underlying molecular mechanisms.
A rat model of chronic LNG exposure was established, and the efficacy of JFP was evaluated based on estrous cycles, serum hormone levels and ovarian morphology. Ovarian transcriptomic analysis and cholesterol-related biochemical assays were performed to investigate the alterations in ovarian cholesterol homeostasis. The role of apolipoprotein A-I (ApoA1) was further examined by using ApoA1 silencing in primary rat ovarian theca cells and intrabursal administration of ApoA1 in vivo. RT-qPCR and Western blotting were subsequently used to validate the key molecular changes and assess the effects of JFP on ApoA1expression, cholesterol homeostasis and the associated signaling pathways.
JFP significantly ameliorated LNG-induced ovarian injury, as evidenced by increased serum levels of FSH, LH and AMH, and decreased estradiol levels and the LH/FSH ratio, reduced cystic follicle formation, and attenuated follicular depletion. Transcriptomic analysis in ovarian tissues, together with cholesterol assays, RT-qPCR and Western blotting, revealed that LNG exposure disrupted ovarian cholesterol homeostasis, with alterations in cholesterol transport and increased ovarian ApoA1 abundance. Intrabursal administration of ApoA1 induced ovarian pathological changes and activated PI3K/Akt signaling in vivo, whereas ApoA1 silencing attenuated PI3K/Akt activation and inhibited the viability of primary ovarian theca cells. JFP markedly reduced ovarian ApoA1 accumulation, improved cholesterol homeostasis, and suppressed PI3K/Akt/NF-κB signaling.
JFP effectively ameliorated ovarian injury induced by long-term LNG exposure in rats, and its protective effects were likely associated with modulation of ApoA1-associated cholesterol homeostasis and suppression of PI3K/Akt signaling.

papers.title: Chaihu-Shugan-San Attenuates Depression by Downregulating Liver LCN2 to Suppress LHb GluN2B-Associated Glutamatergic Signaling.
papers.authors: You X, Song C, Chen W, Zheng Y, Wang R, Liu W et al.
papers.abstract:
The liver-brain axis has emerged as a critical pathway in depression pathogenesis, yet the molecular basis of this crosstalk remains largely unexplored. Chaihu-Shugan-San (CSS), a classic Traditional Chinese Medicine formula for "soothing the liver and relieving depression" has shown both hepatoprotective and antidepressant effects, but whether these actions are linked via the liver-brain axis and through what molecular mechanism remains unknown.
This study aimed to determine whether Chaihu-Shugan-San (CSS) exerts antidepressant effects via the liver-brain axis and to elucidate the mediating role of liver lipocalin 2 (LCN2) and its receptor SLC22A17 in regulating lateral habenula (LHb) function.
A chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) mouse model was established. CSS (2, 4, 8 g/kg) or fluoxetine (10 mg/kg) was orally administered. Depressive-like behaviors were assessed by sucrose preference, open field, and forced swim tests. Hepatic injury was evaluated by serum ALT/AST and H&E staining. Liver transcriptomics and LHb single-cell RNA sequencing were performed to identify key molecules, followed by qRT-PCR, Western blot, ELISA, and immunofluorescence for validation. The causal role of LCN2 was tested via liver-specific AAV-mediated overexpression.
CSS ameliorated CUMS-induced depressive-like behaviors and liver injury. Transcriptomics and PPI network analysis identified Lcn2 as a hub gene. CSS reversed CUMS-induced elevation of LCN2 in the liver, serum, and LHb, as well as the upregulation of its receptor SLC22A17 in the LHb. LHb single-cell sequencing revealed that CSS restored CUMS-induced changes in astrocyte subcluster ASC6, including downregulation of AQP4 and SLC38A1 and impaired intercellular communication. Consequently, CSS reduced the elevated expression of c-FOS and GluN2B and restored AQP4 and SLC38A1 in the LHb. Importantly, liver-specific Lcn2 overexpression recapitulated CUMS-like depressive phenotypes and LHb abnormalities, including elevated SLC22A17 and GluN2B, and largely abolished the antidepressant effects of CSS.
CSS ameliorates depressive-like behaviors in association with downregulation of hepatic LCN2 and its candidate receptor SLC22A17 in the LHb, restoring ASC6-mediated glutamate homeostasis, and suppressing GluN2B-related Glutamatergic Signaling. These findings are consistent with a model in which LHb function may be modulated via the liver-brain axis through hepatic LCN2 and its candidate receptor SLC22A17, although the direct source of LHb LCN2 remains to be determined, offering experimental support for the scientific basis of CSS in "soothing the liver and relieving depression."

papers.title: Siwu Paste alleviates blood deficiency syndrome induced by cyclophosphamide and acetylphenylhydrazine in association with gut microbiota remodeling and improved splenic metabolic homeostasis.
papers.authors: Wan D, Feng X, Xu S, Du Q, Yue W, Zhang S
papers.abstract:
Siwu Paste (SWP), derived from the classical blood-tonifying formula Siwu Decoction, has long been used for blood deficiency-related disorders and has a well-established traditional basis and ethnopharmacological value. Blood deficiency syndrome (BDS) is a common syndrome in traditional Chinese medicine and is associated with impaired blood generation and hematopoietic dysfunction. However, the modern pharmacological mechanisms underlying the beneficial effects of SWP on BDS remain incompletely understood.
This study aims to evaluate the therapeutic effects of SWP on cyclophosphamide and acetylphenylhydrazine induced BDS and to investigate the potential mechanisms underlying its improvement of hematopoietic function.
The chemical constituents of SWP were characterized by ultra-performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole-time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-Q-TOF-MS), and its potential mechanisms were predicted using network pharmacology. An acetylphenylhydrazine (APH)/cyclophosphamide (CTX)-induced BDS rat model was used to evaluate SWP efficacy through flow cytometry, histology, Western blotting, qPCR, 16S rRNA sequencing, and untargeted metabolomics. Broad-spectrum antibiotic treatment, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), and exogenous adenosine diphosphate (ADP) supplementation experiments were performed to evaluate the contribution of the gut microbiota and the involvement of splenic ADP-related metabolic alterations.
SWP significantly improved hematopoietic dysfunction, alleviated systemic inflammation, restored intestinal barrier integrity, reversed the Treg/Th17 imbalance, and reduced apoptosis within the CD45+CD34+ bone marrow cell population in BDS rats. Multi-omics analysis revealed that SWP significantly regulated gut microbiota composition and metabolic profiles; specifically, SWP treatment was associated with a significant increase in the relative abundance of Allobaculum and an upward trend in Lactobacillus, accompanied by a significant reduction in the relative abundance of total ADP in spleen tissue compared with the BDS group. FMT experiments partially transferred the hematopoietic and immunomodulatory effects associated with SWP treatment. Broad-spectrum antibiotic treatment and exogenous ADP supplementation attenuated several SWP-induced improvements in bone-marrow hematopoietic function and Treg/Th17 balance, consistent with the involvement of the gut microbiota-splenic metabolic axis in the therapeutic effects of SWP.
SWP alleviates bone marrow hematopoietic dysfunction in BDS rats, with these effects accompanied by gut microbiota remodeling, restoration of intestinal barrier integrity, suppression of inflammation, and improved metabolic homeostasis. These findings provide modern pharmacological evidence supporting the traditional TCM concept of "treating the marrow via the gut" in blood deficiency-related disorders.

papers.title: Sinensetin inhibits choroidal neovascularization by downregulating the MAPK/ERK pathway.
papers.authors: Han GJ, Du Y, Wu XX, He YX, Lu J, Wang WJ et al.
papers.abstract:
Sinensetin (SIN), a characteristic polymethoxyflavone abundant in Citrus species, is isolated from Citrus peel (Chenpi), a medicinal material widely applied in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) to activate blood circulation and ameliorate blood stasis-associated ocular disorders. Accumulating pharmacological evidence confirms that SIN exerts prominent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-angiogenic bioactivities. It is capable of suppressing pathological angiogenesis in zebrafish and endothelial cell models, which renders SIN a promising candidate for angiogenic ocular diseases. Nevertheless, its therapeutic efficacy against choroidal neovascularization (CNV) remains largely uninvestigated.
This study aimed to investigate the inhibitory effects of SIN on CNV and to dissect the underlying mechanism, specifically focusing on its modulation of FGF1-mediated MAPK/ERK signaling.
The anti-CNV effect of SIN was evaluated both in vitro and in vivo. In vivo, a laser-induced CNV model was established in Brown Norway (BN) rats, and SIN was administered via intravitreal injection; CNV severity was assessed by FITC perfusion, OCT, HE staining, and Western blot. In vitro, human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) were treated with CNV-mimicking ARPE-19 human retinal pigment epithelial cells (ARPE-19) conditioned medium; the effects of SIN on migration and angiogenesis were evaluated by scratch, transwell, and tube formation assays. Combined transcriptomic and proteomic analyses were employed to screen key targets and pathways, and mechanistic validation was performed using the ERK agonist PMA and inhibitor U0126.
In the laser-induced CNV rat model, intravitreal injection of SIN significantly reduced CNV area and thickness and suppressed the MAPK/ERK signaling pathway, effects that were reversed by the ERK agonist PMA. Consistently, in vitro experiments confirmed that SIN dose-dependently reversed the enhanced migration and tube formation of HUVEC induced by CNV-mimicking conditioned medium. Multi-omics analysis identified FGF1 as a shared candidate downstream mediator of SIN, with SIN downregulating FGF1, VEGF-A, HIF-1α, and p-ERK1/2 expression. Further mechanistic studies revealed that the ERK inhibitor U0126 mimicked the anti-angiogenic effect of SIN, whereas the ERK agonist PMA abolished its inhibitory activity, suggesting that SIN exerts anti-CNV effects, at least in part, through suppression of MAPK/ERK signaling.
Collectively, this study demonstrates that citrus-derived SIN exerts anti-CNV effects, at least in part, through suppression of MAPK/ERK signaling, while additional pathways identified by multi-omics may also contribute. These findings highlight SIN as a promising natural product for the treatment of CNV-related ocular diseases, with FGF1 identified as a potential mediator underlying its anti-angiogenic action.

papers.title: Acupuncture attenuates hypertension-induced myocardial hypertrophy: role of the SIRT1/NF-κ B/MAPK signaling axis in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus.
papers.authors: Zhang J, Wu J, Wang P, Wang B, Li S, Luo G et al.
papers.abstract:
Chronic hypertension is a major risk factor for cardiovascular complications and can induce pathological myocardial hypertrophy. The hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN) is a key autonomic regulatory center involved in hypertension through sympathetic overactivation, neuroinflammation, and central renin-angiotensin system dysregulation. Although acupuncture exerts protective effects against hypertension-related target organ damage, its central mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated whether acupuncture was associated with the attenuation of hypertension-induced myocardial hypertrophy in spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs) and whether these effects may involve modulation of the sirtuin 1 (SIRT1)/nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB)/mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling axis in the PVN.
Twenty-seven SHRs were randomly assigned to Model, Acupuncture, and Losartan groups (n = 9 per group), while nine Wistar-Kyoto (WKY) rats served as Controls. Rats received acupuncture at Taichong (LR3), Baihui (GV20), and Sanyinjiao (SP6) or losartan treatment for 12 weeks. Blood pressure, plasma norepinephrine (NE), cardiac function, myocardial remodeling, fibrosis, and PVN-related molecular changes were assessed.
Acupuncture reduced systolic and diastolic blood pressure and decreased plasma NE levels in SHRs. In the PVN, acupuncture increased SIRT1 expression and inhibited NF-κB p65 expression and MAPK phosphorylation. Moreover, acupuncture suppressed central renin-angiotensin system activation, neuroinflammation, and neurotransmitter imbalance by regulating ACE, AT1R, pro-inflammatory cytokines, GABA, and Glu levels. Echocardiographic and histological analyses demonstrated that acupuncture alleviated myocardial hypertrophy, improved cardiac function, and reduced fibrosis and structural remodeling.
Acupuncture was associated with the attenuation of hypertension-induced myocardial hypertrophy in SHRs, possibly involving modulation of the PVN SIRT1/NF-κB/MAPK signaling axis. These effects may involve suppression of neuroinflammation and sympathetic overactivation, regulation of the central renin-angiotensin system, and restoration of PVN neurotransmitter balance, providing new insights into the central neural mechanisms underlying acupuncture-mediated cardioprotection in hypertension.

summary.question: 침치료가 고혈압성 심근비대를 줄이는지와 그 중심 기전이 PVN의 SIRT1/NF-κB/MAPK 신호축과 관련되는지 평가했다.

papers.title: Bilateral Iatrogenic Pneumothorax After Acupuncture in a 26-Year-Old Woman Presenting With Cough, Pleuritic Chest Pain, and Tachycardia: A Case Report.
papers.journal: The American journal of case reports
papers.authors: Nożewski J, Zalewska B, Zwierko B
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Acupuncture is widely used and generally safe, but pneumothorax is a serious complication of needling in the neck, shoulder, or upper back. Bilateral pneumothorax is rare and can present with nonspecific symptoms, delaying diagnosis. This case report highlights the presentation of immediate cough during upper-back needling, delayed presentation with bilateral pneumothorax despite preserved oxygenation, and radiographic regression during specialist-supervised conservative inpatient management. CASE REPORT A 26-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with persistent cough, pleuritic chest pain, and difficulty taking a full breath 2 days after acupuncture in the trapezius region. She was otherwise hemodynamically stable, with a blood pressure of 132/93 mm Hg and oxygen saturation of 100% on room air, but had marked tachycardia (140 beats/min at triage) and decreased right-sided breath sounds. Chest radiography showed bilateral apical pneumothoraces measuring 21 mm on the right and 17 mm on the left. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography excluded pulmonary embolism and confirmed bilateral pneumothoraces up to 23 mm without hemothorax. Preserved blood pressure and oxygenation, absence of respiratory compromise, and availability of specialist inpatient monitoring supported conservative management without pleural intervention. Serial radiographs showed regression to 6 mm on the right and 9 mm on the left before discharge. CONCLUSIONS Recent acupuncture involving the neck, shoulder, or upper back should prompt consideration of pneumothorax in patients with chest pain, cough, dyspnea, or unexplained tachycardia, even when oxygen saturation is normal. Conservative inpatient management may be feasible only in carefully selected patients with bilateral procedure-related pneumothorax under close specialist clinical and radiographic surveillance.

papers.title: Efficacy and Mechanism of Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation in Patients With Poststroke Dysphagia: Protocol for a Randomized, Sham-Controlled Clinical Trial.
papers.authors: Gao L, Li J, Xie M, Xu C, Zhang C, Kuang W et al.
papers.abstract:
Dysphagia is a common complication following stroke. While current management strategies for poststroke dysphagia (PSD) range from nutritional support to neurostimulation techniques, an optimal treatment regimen remains elusive. As a promising noninvasive neuromodulation approach, transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) requires further validation in rigorously designed trials to establish robust evidence of its efficacy and mechanisms of action.
This study aims to validate the efficacy of taVNS in treating PSD and to elucidate its underlying mechanisms, thereby supporting the development of a novel, noninvasive therapeutic strategy for improving swallowing function in stroke survivors.
This study will use a prospective, randomized, double-blind, controlled trial design. A total of 40 patients with PSD will be enrolled and randomly allocated to either a taVNS group or a sham taVNS group. Both groups will receive conventional swallowing rehabilitation therapy as the baseline intervention. The taVNS group will receive bilateral electrical stimulation at the cymba conchae and cavum conchae of the auricle. These sites correspond to the "Heart" and "Kidney" auricular acupoints, selected in accordance with traditional Chinese medicine theory. In contrast, the sham taVNS group will receive stimulation at regions of the auricle not innervated by the vagus nerve. The primary outcome measure will be the Penetration-Aspiration Scale score. Secondary outcomes will include the Yale Pharyngeal Residue Severity Rating Scale, hyoid bone displacement and hyoid-thyroid approximation distance assessed via B-mode ultrasonography, and motor-evoked potentials of the suprahyoid muscles elicited by transcranial magnetic stimulation. All outcome measures will be evaluated at baseline and after the 2-week intervention period.
This paper describes the protocol for a study evaluating the efficacy and mechanisms of taVNS in patients with PSD. The study was funded in January 2025. Participant recruitment began in March 2025 and is projected to conclude by October 2026. Data collection began in March 2025 and is projected to be completed by October 2026. Primary study results are expected to be submitted for publication in winter 2026.
This study aims to validate the efficacy of taVNS in treating PSD and to elucidate its underlying mechanisms, thereby supporting the development of a novel, noninvasive therapeutic strategy for improving swallowing function in stroke survivors.

papers.title: Notoginsenoside R2 Antagonizes Renal Interstitial Fibrosis by Regulating Fatty Acid Oxidation via the CASP2/ALDH3A1 Axis.
papers.authors: Chen G, Li T, Wang Z, Zhao H, Xun X, Wang Y et al.
papers.abstract: Renal interstitial fibrosis (RIF) is a major driver of chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression, yet effective therapies remain limited. The Shen-Yan-Fang-Shuai formula (SYFSF) exhibits clinical renoprotective effects; however, its active components and mechanisms remain unclear. This study identifies notoginsenoside R2 (NGR2) as a core active compound of SYFSF that directly binds to caspase-2 (CASP2). Integrative multi-omics analyses in unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO) rats and transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)-induced NRK-52E cells demonstrate that NGR2 upregulates CASP2, enhances the CASP2-aldehyde dehydrogenase 3 family member A1 (ALDH3A1) interaction, and promotes ALDH3A1 deubiquitination, thereby stabilizing ALDH3A1. This stabilization restores the integrity of mitochondria-associated endoplasmic reticulum membranes (MAMs) and improves fatty acid oxidation (FAO) by upregulating carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1A (CPT1A), acyl-CoA dehydrogenase long chain (ACADL), and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor α (PPARα). It also reduces lipid accumulation, oxidative stress, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), inflammation, and collagen deposition. In vivo, NGR2 ameliorates renal dysfunction and fibrosis. Mechanistically, NGR2 binds the caspase activation and recruitment domain (CARD) of CASP2 without occluding the ubiquitin-interacting motif-like (UIML) region required for its deubiquitinase function, thereby increasing CASP2 abundance and stability rather than activating its apoptotic protease activity, and facilitating ubiquitin chain removal from ALDH3A1. These findings demonstrate that SYFSF and NGR2 antagonize RIF by targeting the CASP2/ALDH3A1 axis to restore MAM function and FAO, providing a molecular basis for traditional Chinese medicine in CKD therapy.

papers.title: Piezo1-mitochondrial calcium uniporter coupling-dependent mechanotransduction basis for acupuncture to drive analgesia.
papers.authors: Yao K, Xia J, Dou B, Fan Z, Forhad SM, Chen Z et al.
papers.abstract:
The mechanosensitive ion channel Piezo1 is a critical sensor of mechanical forces in diverse biological contexts, albeit its role in translating the acupuncture-induced mechanical stimulation into analgesic signaling remains largely unexplored. Acupuncture is a widely used therapy for pain management, with needle manipulation-generated mechanical forces considered central to its therapeutic efficacy. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying this mechanotransduction process remain unknown. Here, we identified myocyte Piezo1 at the ST36 acupoint as a key initiator converting local needling force into peripherally derived analgesic signaling under complete Freund's adjuvant (CFA)-induced inflammatory pain conditions.
In mice with CFA-induced inflammatory pain, we assessed the analgesic efficacy of deep needling at ST36 using paw withdrawal latency tests. The underlying molecular mechanisms were examined through immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, western blotting, transmission electron microscopy, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, electromyography, and in vivo two-photon calcium (Ca) imaging. To evaluate the Piezo1-Ca2⁺-calmodulin (CaM)-Ca2⁺/CaM-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII)-signaling axis and its downstream effects on mitochondrial function and purinergic signaling, we employed muscle-specific adeno-associated virus-mediated knockdown of Piezo1 and CaM together with a panel of pharmacological modulators (GsMTx4, Yoda1, TFP, 2-APB, RU360, DPCPX).
We first confirmed Piezo1 expression in myocytes within the ST36 acupoint, and muscle-specific Piezo1 knockdown abrogated the analgesic effects of deep needling at ST36. Mechanical stimulation by needling activated Piezo1, thereby triggering Ca2⁺ influx, increasing CaM expression and CaMKII phosphorylation, and enhancing sarcoplasmic reticulum-mitochondrial coupling via the inositol trisphosphate receptor-1 (IP3R1)-glucose-regulated protein 75 (GRP75)-voltage-dependent anion channel-1 (VDAC1) complex and mitochondrial Ca uniporter (MCU) pathway. These events promoted mitochondrial Ca2⁺ uptake and increased adenosine triphosphate (ATP)/adenosine production. Both genetic and pharmacological inhibition of Piezo1, CaM, or downstream signaling molecules blocked the analgesic effects of acupuncture, whereas direct Piezo1 activation with Yoda1 mimicked these effects. In vivo two-photon Ca imaging confirmed that electroacupuncture-evoked myocyte Ca2⁺ transients are Piezo1-dependent, and the resulting adenosine may mediate remote analgesia through the activation of the adenosine A1 receptor.
Piezo1 acts as a core peripheral mechanotransducer that converts local mechanical stimuli generated by acupuncture into downstream analgesic signaling in CFA-induced inflammatory pain. This study delineates a specific myocyte-originated mechanotransduction axis underlying acupuncture analgesia under inflammatory conditions, thereby providing mechanistic insights for understanding acupoint-specific therapeutic effects.

papers.title: Traditional herbal medicine Hyangsapyeongwi-san inhibits alcohol-induced gastric injury in mice by regulating NLRP3 inflammasome signaling.
papers.authors: Huh E, Ju IG, Kim SH, Kang M, Lee S, Park H et al.
papers.abstract:
Hyangsapyeongwi-san (HPS), known as Xiangsha Pingwei San in Chinese medicine, is a classical herbal formula composed of ten medicinal herbs that has been traditionally used in traditional Korean medicine and East Asian medicine for centuries to treat gastrointestinal disorders associated with digestive impairment, including functional dyspepsia and gastritis. In traditional Korean medicine theory, these conditions correspond to "dampness-heat accumulation" and "qi stagnation" patterns affecting the spleen and stomach. HPS is formulated to "eliminate dampness, strengthen the spleen, and regulate qi circulation"-a traditional rationale for which the present study provides molecular evidence by demonstrating suppression of key inflammatory signaling pathways underlying gastric mucosal injury.
This study aimed to investigate the gastroprotective effects of HPS against acute gastric injury and to elucidate its underlying molecular mechanisms, with a focus on NLRP3 inflammasome activation.
Male ICR mice were administered HPS (75 or 300 mg/kg) or ranitidine (40 mg/kg) orally once daily for 4 days prior to HCl/ethanol-induced gastric injury. Gastric damage, NLRP3 inflammasome components, inflammatory cytokines, signaling pathways, and apoptosis markers were assessed. Anti-inflammatory effects were further evaluated in TNF-α-stimulated MKN45 gastric epithelial cells.
HPS dose-dependently reduced gastric damage scores and preserved mucosal architecture. High-dose HPS significantly suppressed IL-1β protein, IL-1β mRNA, and TNF-α mRNA expression. HPS inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome activation by reducing NLRP3 and caspase-1 levels, suppressed AKT and NF-κB p65 phosphorylation, and prevented apoptosis. In gastric epithelial cells, HPS attenuated IL-6 and IL-8 expression without cytotoxicity.
HPS protects against acute gastric injury through NLRP3 inflammasome inhibition via the AKT/NF-κB pathway, providing molecular evidence that supports its traditional use for digestive disorders.

papers.title: Sanwu Huangqin decoction induces ferroptosis in colorectal cancer cells by triggering NCOA4/FTH1-mediated ferritinophagy.
papers.authors: Tan X, Jiang R, Shan K, Liu J, Yu H, Han R et al.
papers.abstract:
In traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), colorectal cancer (CRC) is commonly associated with patterns such as damp-heat accumulation, heat toxin, and yin deficiency. Sanwu Huangqin Decoction (SWHQD) is a classical traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formula composed of three medicinal herbs-Huangqin (Scutellaria baicalensis Georgi), Kushen (Sophora flavescens Ait.), and Dihuang (Rehmannia glutinosa Libosch.). It has been traditionally prescribed for clearing heat, eliminating dampness, and nourishing yin, particularly in the treatment of gastrointestinal disorders. Clinically, SWHQD has been used as an adjunctive intervention for CRC management. However, the precise pharmacological mechanisms underlying its anti-CRC activity remain incompletely characterized.
This study sought to evaluate the anti-tumorigenic efficacy of SWHQD against CRC and to determine whether ferritinophagy-mediated ferroptosis contributes to its mechanism of action.
Human CRC cell lines (HCT116 and SW480) and a xenograft tumor model in BALB/c nude mice were used to evaluate the anti-tumor effects of SWHQD in vitro and in vivo. Ferroptosis-related indicators, including intracellular Fe2+, lipid reactive oxygen species (ROS), malondialdehyde (MDA), and glutathione (GSH), were measured. The role of ferritinophagy was examined through analysis of the NCOA4/FTH1 pathway and NCOA4 gene silencing.
SWHQD significantly suppressed CRC cell proliferation in vitro and inhibited tumor growth in vivo. Treatment induced hallmark features of ferroptosis, including elevated intracellular Fe2+, increased lipid ROS and MDA levels, and depletion of GSH, all of which were significantly abrogated by the ferroptosis inhibitors. Mechanistically, SWHQD upregulated nuclear receptor coactivator 4 (NCOA4), strengthened the interaction between NCOA4 and ferritin heavy chain 1 (FTH1), promoted autophagic degradation of FTH1, and consequently triggered iron release, thereby activating ferritinophagy-dependent ferroptosis. Silencing of NCOA4 markedly attenuated these biochemical and functional responses.
SWHQD suppresses CRC through a mechanism involving the NCOA4/FTH1 pathway to induce ferritinophagy-dependent ferroptosis. These findings provide mechanistic evidence supporting the traditional application of SWHQD and highlight its potential as a complementary therapeutic strategy for CRC.

papers.title: Smilacis Chinae Rhizoma ethyl acetate fraction alleviates IMQ-induced psoriasis by inhibiting IL-17-driven T-cell immune responses.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Wei F, Guo Y, Tang S, Zhang H, Jin L et al.
papers.abstract:
Smilacis Chinae Rhizoma (SCR), derived from the rhizome of Smilax china L., has long been utilized in traditional Chinese medicine for the treatment of inflammatory dermatological disorders, including cutaneous abscesses.
This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic potential and underlying mechanisms of Smilacis Chinae Rhizoma ethyl acetate fraction (SCR-EA) in psoriasis, with a focus on its immunomodulatory effects on T-cell responses and the IL-17 signaling pathway.
A psoriasis-like mouse model was induced via topical imiquimod (IMQ) application. Mice were treated with SCR-EA (100 or 200 mg/kg) or methotrexate (MTX, 1 mg/kg). Psoriasis severity was assessed using the Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI). Histopathological alterations, KC proliferation, and inflammatory cytokine mRNA levels (IL-6, TGF-β1, IL-1β, S100A9) were analyzed. T-cell subset distribution in the spleen was examined by flow cytometry. Key IL-17 pathway proteins (IL-17A, RORγt, p-STAT3, STAT3) were assessed by Western blot. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were used to predict potential targets and pathways, followed by experimental validation.
SCR-EA significantly alleviated IMQ-induced psoriatic lesions, reduced epidermal thickness, and inhibited KC hyperproliferation. It suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokine expression and corrected the IMQ-induced imbalance of Th1, Th2, and Th17 cell subsets in the spleen. Network pharmacology identified the IL-17 signaling pathway as a major target, which was validated by SCR-EA's inhibition of IL-17A, RORγt, and STAT3 activation. Molecular docking revealed strong binding affinities between SCR-EA's primary constituents (astilbin, engeletin, resveratrol) and IL-6 and TNF-α.
SCR-EA mitigates IMQ-induced psoriasis by modulating T-cell differentiation and inhibiting the IL-17 signaling pathway. This study provides a pharmacological foundation for the traditional use of SCR in treating inflammatory skin conditions and positions SCR-EA as a promising multi-target candidate for psoriasis therapy.

papers.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials on the efficacy of Shensong Yangxin capsule for recurrence of atrial fibrillation after catheter ablation.
papers.authors: Mao T, Li Y, Chen J, Qu X, Cheng B, Xie L et al.
papers.abstract:
Shensong Yangxin (SSYX) capsule, a well-known Chinese patent medicine, is widely applied in the treatment of atrial fibrillation (AF).
To determine the efficacy and safety of SSYX as adjunctive therapy on recurrence after ablation in AF patients.
A systematic search was conducted across eight databases to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving SSYX therapy after first AF ablation until 1st July 2025. The primary outcome was AF recurrence, and safety endpoint was also examined. The quality of evidence was assessed using the GRADE framework. The protocol was prospectively registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251012453).
Nine studies comprising 2199 patients were included. Anti-arrhythmic drugs (AADs) plus SSYX reduced early recurrence by 45% (RR 0.55, 95% CI: 0.42 to 0.71, P < 0.001; I2 = 0%) in overall AF populations, and late recurrence by 38% (RR 0.62, 95% CI: 0.47 to 0.81, P < 0.001; I2 = 0%) in persistent AF. Moreover, no statistically significant difference was observed in the incidence of adverse events between SSYX and control groups. A moderate and low level of evidence were identified for late and early recurrence, separately.
Combination therapy with AAD and SSYX after ablation could safely and effectively reduce early recurrence across AF populations and late recurrence only for persistent AF. This evidence highlights the potential of SSYX as a potential adjuvant treatment option after AF ablation. However, extrapolation to Western populations requires caution.

papers.title: A multidimensional integrated strategy for identifying anti-thrombotic quality markers(Q-Markers) in Taohong Siwu decoction through combined analysis of chemical profiling, bioactivity, and pharmacodynamic efficacy.
papers.authors: Yang R, Wu Y, He L, Li R, Yang W, Feng Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Taohong Siwu Decoction (TSD), originating from the Qing Dynasty medical text Gynecology Ice Mirror, is a representative formula for treating blood stasis syndrome, with the effects of promoting blood circulation, nourishing blood, and resolving stasis. Following this lead, modern research has revealed that the formula exerts antithrombotic effects through multiple pathways, thereby providing a critical pharmacological basis for its function of "promoting blood circulation and removing blood stasis". However, the pharmacodynamic material basis underlying this efficacy awaits further clarification.
This study aims to establish a multidimensional spectrum-effect correlation model for TSD by integrating its chemical composition with relevant biological activity and antithrombotic efficacy. The goal is to identify quality markers (Q-Markers) that are closely associated with its effects of promoting blood circulation and resolving blood stasis.
UPLC-QqQ-MS/MS was used to quantify 31 components in TSD. Its biological activity was assessed via in vitro anticoagulant and antiplatelet assays, and efficacy via a zebrafish thrombosis model. The study employed grey relational analysis (GRA) and backpropagation neural networks (BP-ANN) to analyze component-activity, activity-efficacy, and component-efficacy correlations. It also constructed a TSD antithrombotic component-target-pathway network via bioinformatics and molecular docking, identifying potential active components. Validation via zebrafish models and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) confirmed TSD's multi-component and multi-target interactions, ultimately determining its antithrombotic Q-Markers.
Thirty-one compounds across 15 TSD batches were quantified. Systematic cluster analysis categorized the batches into four groups, with Rehmannia glutinosa (Gaertn.) Libosch. ex DC. root quality identified as the main factor affecting TSD's quality consistency. The study confirmed TSD's in vitro anticoagulant and antiplatelet aggregation activity, as well as its satisfactory thrombus inhibition rate in zebrafish models. By combining GRA and BP-ANN, the study identified 19 key components; through molecular docking and experimental validation, six compounds were screened out: rehmannioside D, amygdalin, paeoniflorin, ferulic acid, hydroxysafflor yellow A, and chlorogenic acid. These six components exhibited strong binding affinity to thrombosis-related targets including GAPDH, IL-6, AKT1, CASP3, and EGFR, and were finally confirmed as Q-Markers for TSD's blood circulation-promoting and stasis-resolving efficacy.
Via multidimensional spectrum-effect correlation analysis, this study identified TSD's blood circulation-promoting Q-Markers. These findings lay a foundation for TSD's quality standards/clinical application and provide a reference for traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) constituent-pharmacology research.

papers.title: Discovery of a Piezo1-targeting polysaccharide from marine squid ink with dual barrier-repair and anti-inflammatory activities against atopic dermatitis.
papers.authors: Wen X, Liu X, Huang T, Deng Q, Huang H, Zhou X et al.
papers.abstract:
Squid ink has been documented in traditional Chinese medicine, notably in the ancient text Ben Jing, for its use in treating wounds, gastric disorders, and skin lesions, suggesting its potential as a source of bioactive compounds for dermatological applications.
This study aimed to isolate and structurally characterize a novel polysaccharide from the ink of the cuttlefish Symplectoteuthis oualaniensis (SIP) and to evaluate its therapeutic potential and mechanism of action against atopic dermatitis (AD).
SIP was extracted, purified, and characterized using HPGPC, monosaccharide analysis, FT-IR, and NMR. Its effects were assessed in a TNF-α/IFN-γ-induced HaCaT keratinocyte inflammation model and a 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene (DNCB)-induced murine AD model. Key markers of barrier function and inflammation were analyzed by qPCR, Western blot, and immunohistochemistry. The interaction with the mechanosensitive ion channel Piezo1 was investigated through molecular docking, dynamics simulations, calcium imaging, and functional assays.
Structural analysis revealed SIP as a unique polysaccharide with a weight-average molecular weight of ∼30 kDa. In vitro, SIP significantly upregulated barrier proteins (filaggrin and involucrin) and suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokines (TSLP and IL-8). In AD-like mice, topical SIP application ameliorated clinical severity, restored epidermal integrity, reduced immune cell infiltration, and decreased levels of TSLP, TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-4, and IL-13. Mechanistically, SIP directly bound to and inhibited Piezo1, thereby attenuating Ca2+ influx, NFAT1 nuclear translocation, and subsequent TSLP production.
The polysaccharide SIP from squid ink exerts dual barrier-repair and anti-inflammatory effects in AD by targeting the Piezo1-Ca2+-NFAT1-TSLP axis. This work validates the ethnopharmacological relevance of a traditional marine resource and identifies a novel natural-product mechanism for ameliorating inflammatory skin disease.

papers.title: Investigating the potential active components and mechanisms of Xiongcan Yishen formula in treating late-onset hypogonadism using network pharmacology combined with metabolomics and absorbed components.
papers.authors: Wang H, Jian M, Liu W, Yang C, Peng A, Wu H et al.
papers.abstract:
Xiongcan Yishen formula (XCYSF) is a traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formula used for the treatment of male late-onset hypogonadism (LOH). However, its active components and underlying mechanisms remain unclear.
To investigate the potential pharmacodynamic material basis and mechanisms of XCYSF against LOH by integrating serum pharmacochemistry, network pharmacology, and metabolomics.
The blood-entry components of XCYSF in rat serum were identified using UPLC-Q-TOF-MS. Network pharmacology was employed to predict the targets of these components as well as LOH-related targets. Metabolomics was performed to analyze differential serum metabolites in a cyclophosphamide-induced LOH rat model. Integrated analyses were conducted to identify core targets and pathways, which were further validated by molecular docking. In vivo experiments were carried out using a LOH rat model, and in vitro experiments were performed using H2O2-induced TM3 cells.
A total of 31 blood-entry components were identified, corresponding to 255 potential targets associated with LOH. Metabolomics analysis revealed 48 differential metabolites, mainly involved in metabolic pathways such as glycerophospholipid metabolism, bile acid metabolism, and autophagy. Integrative analysis focused on the PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway and four core targets: AR, mTOR, GSK3β, and APP. In vivo experiments demonstrated that XCYSF restored testosterone levels in LOH rats and exerted therapeutic effects by inhibiting the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway. In vitro, XCYSF-containing serum and its potential key component, tribuloside, promoted testosterone secretion through inhibition of the same pathway.
XCYSF and its active component tribuloside promote testosterone synthesis and alleviate LOH by inhibiting the PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway.

papers.title: Tangeretin, a bioactive polymethoxyflavone from immature Citrus aurantium L. fruit, ameliorates experimental colitis by targeting the macrophage β2 integrin Mac-1.
papers.authors: Zhu J, Zhu X, Lin X, Zhou Q, Chen W, Liu Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Zhiqiao, the dried immature fruit of Citrus aurantium L., is a traditional Chinese medicine widely used for treating gastrointestinal disorders. Among its varieties, Quzhiqiao, a geo-authentic herb from Quzhou, China, is highly valued for its superior quality, yet the pharmacological basis for its efficacy in inflammatory bowel disease remains unclear.
This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects and underlying molecular mechanisms of the ethanol extract of Quzhiqiao (QZCEE) and its key bioactive compound in a mouse model of ulcerative colitis (UC), with a focus on its impact on macrophage-driven inflammation.
The efficacy of orally administered QZCEE and its constituent, tangeretin, was evaluated in a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis mouse model by assessing clinical (DAI score) and pathological (colon length, histology) parameters. Intestinal barrier integrity was examined by Western blot and qPCR. Macrophage infiltration and colonic inflammatory responses were measured by immunohistochemistry, ELISA, and qPCR. The effects of QZCEE and tangeretin on macrophage adhesion, migration, and chemotaxis were assessed in vitro using bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs). The molecular target was identified and validated through molecular docking, pull-down, cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS) assay, and Microscale Thermophoresis (MST) assays. The downstream signaling pathway was investigated by Western blot and Rac1 activation assays.
Oral administration of QZCEE significantly ameliorated the severity of DSS-induced colitis, evidenced by reduced DAI scores, restored colon length, and alleviated histological damage. QZCEE also repaired the intestinal barrier by upregulating the expression of tight junction proteins ZO-1 and Occludin. Mechanistically, QZCEE markedly suppressed the infiltration of F4/80+ macrophages into the inflamed colon and inhibited the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6). Intriguingly, QZCEE did not reduce colonic CCL2 levels but directly inhibited macrophage chemotaxis in vitro. Tangeretin, a polymethoxyflavone in QZCEE, was identified as the key bioactive compound responsible for this effect. We provided compelling evidence that tangeretin directly binds to the β2 integrin Mac-1 (αMβ2) with a dissociation constant (Kd) of 3.87 μM, thereby blocking its interaction with ICAM-1 and suppressing the downstream Vav1/Rac1 signaling pathway. Importantly, oral administration of tangeretin alone recapitulated the therapeutic and immunomodulatory effects of the QZCEE extract in vivo.
Our findings demonstrate that the geo-authentic herb Quzhiqiao exerts potent anti-colitis effects. This therapeutic action is primarily mediated by its bioactive compound, tangeretin, which functions as a novel, direct antagonist of the β2 integrin Mac-1. By blocking macrophage recruitment, tangeretin represents a promising natural lead compound for the development of targeted therapies for UC. This study provides a robust scientific rationale for the ethnopharmacological use of Quzhiqiao and unveils a precise molecular mechanism for its efficacy.

papers.title: Xijiao Dihuang decoction ameliorates sepsis by regulating macrophage polarization via activation of the itaconate-mediated Nrf2/HO-1 pathway.
papers.authors: Ge F, Zhu Y, Xu L, Zhao X, Wang D, Tian F et al.
papers.abstract:
Sepsis is a leading cause of mortality in critically ill patients and is predominantly triggered by infection. Xijiao Dihuang Decoction (XJDH), a classic traditional Chinese medicine formula, has demonstrated clinical efficacy in the early intervention of sepsis. However, its underlying mechanism remains to be elucidated.
This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects of XJDH on sepsis and its potential molecular mechanism.
A sepsis mouse model was established by intraperitoneal injection of lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Systemic inflammation was assessed using ELISA and hematological analysis. Histopathological damage in multiple organs was evaluated by hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining, and the expression of macrophage polarization markers (CD86 and CD206) was detected by immunofluorescence staining. In vitro, an LPS-stimulated THP-1 cell model was employed to further validate the regulatory effects of XJDH on macrophage polarization and inflammatory responses. The expression of Irg1, Nrf2, and HO-1 was examined using Western blot and qRT-PCR to explore the potential molecular mechanism.
In vivo experiments demonstrated that XJDH significantly ameliorated systemic symptoms, alleviated inflammatory responses and multi-organ damage, and promoted macrophage polarization towards the M2 phenotype in septic mice. Following administration of the itaconate inhibitor (Irg1-IN-1), the inflammatory response showed no improvement. In vitro experiments further confirmed that XJDH dose-dependently promoted the phenotypic switch of LPS-induced THP-1 cells from M1 to M2, downregulated pro-inflammatory cytokines, and upregulated anti-inflammatory cytokines. This mechanism involved XJDH-mediated upregulation of Irg1 expression and activation of the Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway.
This study is the first to demonstrate that XJDH alleviates inflammatory responses and multi-organ damage in sepsis by activating the itaconate-mediated Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway to regulate macrophage polarization, thereby providing a new scientific basis for its clinical application.

papers.title: Lobetyolin reinforces endothelial cytoskeletal integrity to alleviate Pseudomonas aeruginosa-induced acute lung injury via targeting ACTN1.
papers.authors: Zhang J, Wang Z, Wang S, Yan Y, Wang X, Zhang M et al.
papers.abstract:
Codonopsis Radix (CR), known as Dangshen in traditional Chinese medicine,is frequently used to tonify Qi and strengthen the spleen and lung. Clinically, "Lung-Qi deficiency" manifests as respiratory weakness and susceptibility to infection. The traditional action of "consolidating Qi to protect the exterior" parallels the physiological preservation of the pulmonary endothelial barrier. However, the bioactive basis linking this traditional efficacy to barrier reinforcement remains unclear.
This study evaluates the protective effects of CR against Pseudomonas aeruginosa-induced acute lung injury (ALI), identifies the primary bioactive component responsible for barrier protection, and elucidates its molecular mechanism involving cytoskeletal stabilization.
A P. aeruginosa-induced ALI mouse model was established to assess the efficacy of CR extract (CRE) and its polyacetylene glycoside, lobetyolin (LBT). Lung injury severity, inflammatory responses, and endothelial barrier function were systematically evaluated. Bioactivity-guided fractionation screened for active constituents. The mechanism was investigated using integrated transcriptomics, chemical proteomics, and molecular docking, validated by in vitro and in vivo experiments.
Both CRE and LBT significantly attenuated lung histopathology, diminished pulmonary edema, and suppressed leukocyte infiltration and pro-inflammatory cytokine production. LBT was identified as the key bioactive constituent restoring endothelial barrier integrity, evidenced by upregulated expression and junctional localization of VE-Cadherin, ZO-1, and Claudin-5. Mechanistically, LBT directly targets α-actinin-1 (ACTN1). Functioning as a "molecular stabilizer", LBT enhances ACTN1-F-actin affinity, promoting cortical actin organization and stabilizing intercellular junctions under inflammatory stress.
This study identifies LBT as a novel structural consolidator of the vascular endothelial barrier. By demonstrating that LBT reinforces endothelial cytoskeletal organization via ACTN1, our findings offer a compelling modern scientific interpretation of the traditional efficacy of CR in "tonifying Lung-Qi": physically strengthening the biological barrier. Furthermore, targeting ACTN1-mediated cytoskeleton modulation presents a promising strategy for treating ALI and vascular leakage disorders.

papers.title: Clinacanthus nutans (Burm. f.) Lindau ameliorates type 2 diabetes mellitus by suppressing chemokine-mediated inflammation and apoptosis in pancreatic β-cells: An integrated multi-omics study.
papers.authors: Zhang L, Yan Z, Wang X, Han X, Ma T, Yuan Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is characterized by chronic hyperglycemia and metabolic dysregulation, in which pancreatic β-cell dysfunction and local chronic inflammation are key drivers of disease progression. Clinacanthus nutans (Burm. f.) Lindau (CN) is a traditional medicinal plant with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities; however, the mechanism underlying its protective effects on pancreatic β-cells in T2DM remains unclear.
This study aimed to systematically identify the blood-absorbed constituents of CN and, by integrating multi-omics analyses and in vivo and in vitro experiments, to investigate its pharmacological effects against T2DM and the underlying mechanism by which CN ameliorates islet inflammation and apoptosis via regulation of the chemokine signaling pathways in β-cells.
UHPLC-QTOF-MS was employed to identify the chemical constituents of CN extracts and their prototypes absorbed into the bloodstream. Network pharmacology analysis was performed based on the identified compounds to construct the protein-protein interaction and compound-target networks. Representative binding conformations were subjected to molecular docking and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate binding stability. Transcriptomic sequencing of cellular samples, combined with enrichment analysis, was conducted to elucidate key signaling pathways. The effects of CN were further evaluated in a high-fat diet and streptozotocin-induced T2DM mouse model by assessing glucose metabolism, pancreatic morphology, and markers of inflammation and apoptosis. In MIN6 cells exposed to high-glucose (HG) and palmitic acid (PA) conditions, CN-containing serum (CN-CS) was used to validate its effects on cell viability, insulin secretion, chemokine expression, inflammation, and apoptosis.
UHPLC-QTOF-MS identified 45 prototype compounds derived from CN in the serum. Both network pharmacology and transcriptomic enrichment analyses consistently indicated that the chemokine signaling pathway, along with inflammation- and apoptosis-related pathways, played dominant roles in the pharmacological actions of CN. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations demonstrated that several major constituents formed stable interactions with key inflammatory proteins such as TNF-α and IL-1β. In vivo experiments showed that CN dose-dependently improved fasting blood glucose levels, OGTT/ITT indices, and partially restored islet morphology in diabetic mice. Moreover, CN significantly reduced the expression of inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-18) and chemokines (CCL2, CXCL12) in tissues and serum, while suppressing the abnormal expression of apoptosis-related proteins. In vitro experiments showed that 15% CN-CS significantly restored the viability of MIN6 cells exposed to HG/PA conditions, promoted insulin secretion, modulated CCL2 and CXCL12 expression, thereby reducing inflammatory cytokine expression, attenuated apoptosis, and restored pancreatic β-cell function.
This study is the first to demonstrate that flavonoids, phenols, terpenoids, phenylpropanoids, and alkaloids are the key active constituents of CN. This traditional herbal medicine exerts its pharmacological effects by modulating the chemokine signaling pathway in β-cells, thereby suppressing inflammatory responses and apoptosis, significantly improving pancreatic β-cell function, and restoring metabolic homeostasis. This study provides a systematic basis for elucidating the mechanisms of CN as a natural multi-target candidate agent and offers new theoretical insights into the development of chemokine pathway-targeted strategies for the prevention and treatment of T2DM.

papers.title: Lishui Xiaozhong granules protect against diabetic retinopathy by activating PINK1/parkin-mediated mitophagy and suppressing ferroptosis.
papers.authors: Yu D, Yongjian T, Yali Q, Jianwei W, Chuanhong J
papers.abstract:
Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a severe microvascular complication of diabetes that is closely associated with hyperglycemia-induced mitochondrial dysfunction. Lishui Xiaozhong granules (LSXZ) are an empirical traditional Chinese medicine used to treat DR. However, its precise molecular targets and underlying mechanisms remain unclear.
This study investigated whether LSXZ protects retinal cells under hyperglycemic conditions by regulating PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy.
Human Müller cells were exposed to high glucose (HG; 50 mM) to establish an in vitro model and treated with LSXZ-containing serum and the mitophagy inhibitor cyclosporin A (CsA). Genetic knockdown via siRNA was performed to validate the necessity of the PINK1/Parkin pathway. A zebrafish DR model was induced using an HG, high-fat diet, and treated with different LSXZ concentrations. Cell viability, mitophagy, apoptosis, ferroptosis, mitochondrial function, and ultrastructural changes were assessed using CCK-8 assays, western blotting, qPCR, immunofluorescence, and transmission electron microscopy. Retinal histopathology, vascular diameter, inflammatory cell activation, oxidative stress, and gene expression profiles in zebrafish were assessed using hematoxylin-eosin staining, fluorescence microscopy, and transcriptomic sequencing.
LSXZ treatment reversed pathological changes by restoring PINK1/Parkin signaling, elevating LC3-II/LC3-I ratio, enhancing mitochondrial function, and suppressing apoptosis and ferroptosis-effects partially attenuated by CsA. Mitophagosomes increased after LSXZ treatment. Crucially, specific knockdown of PINK1 or Parkin significantly abolished LSXZ-induced cytoprotection, reversing the regulation of apoptotic/ferroptotic markers and mitochondrial recovery, thereby confirming the pivotal necessity of this pathway.​ In zebrafish, LSXZ alleviated hyperglycemia-induced retinal inner nuclear layer thinning, vascular dilation, excessive macrophage/astrocyte activation, and oxidative stress. These protective effects were mediated through upregulation of the TOMM40/TOMM20-PINK1/Parkin-MFN2 axis.

papers.title: Realgar transforming solution suppresses KG-1a-derived CD34+CD38- acute myeloid leukemia stem cell-like phenotypes in association with ER-mitochondrial stress and mitophagy-related alterations.
papers.authors: Wang T, Liu W, Lyu C, Luo Y, Tang X, Han C et al.
papers.abstract:
Realgar is an arsenic-containing mineral medicine and a key component of Realgar-Indigo naturalis formula, an oral traditional Chinese medicine preparation clinically used in China for acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL), a biologically distinct subtype of acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Realgar Transforming Solution (RTS) is a microbially processed realgar preparation. Its activity in AML stem cell-like contexts outside APL remains insufficiently defined, particularly in cell-line-derived CD34+CD38- LSC-like models.
To evaluate whether RTS suppresses stemness-associated phenotypic features in KG-1a-derived CD34+CD38- LSC-like cells and to explore its association with endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS), mitochondrial injury, and mitophagy-related alterations.
CD34+CD38- LSC-like cells were enriched from KG-1a cells and used as a cell-line-derived in vitro model. Cell viability, apoptosis, cell cycle, CD34+CD38- fraction, colony formation, and TIM3/HAVCR2 expression were assessed after RTS treatment. RNA sequencing, Ca2+ measurement, ROS detection, mitochondrial membrane potential assay, MDC staining, western blotting, RT-qPCR, immunofluorescence, and transmission electron microscopy were performed. 4-phenylbutyric acid and Mdivi-1 were used as pharmacological rescue agents.
RTS reduced the CD34+CD38- fraction, colony formation, and TIM3/HAVCR2 expression, while inducing apoptosis in KG-1a-derived LSC-like cells. Transcriptomics implicated ER protein processing, unfolded protein response, apoptosis, autophagy, and mitophagy-related pathways. RTS increased Ca2+ levels, ROS accumulation, mitochondrial depolarization, PERK-eIF2α-ATF4-CHOP signaling, and PINK1/Parkin-associated mitophagy-like marker changes. 4-phenylbutyric acid and Mdivi-1 partially rescued RTS-impaired LSC-like phenotypic features, supporting pathway involvement.
RTS suppressed stemness-associated phenotypic features in a KG-1a-derived CD34+CD38- LSC-like model. These effects were associated with ERS, mitochondrial injury, and PINK1/Parkin-related mitophagy-like alterations.

papers.title: Analgesic and Sedative Effect of Acupuncture Combined with Medicine on Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery.
papers.authors: Huang B, Ding H, Liang W, Xu L
papers.abstract: Acupuncture (AP) has been reported to modulate inflammation and oxidative stress, but whether it can reduce dexmedetomidine (Dex) requirements or protect against Dex-induced diaphragm toxicity during mechanical ventilation (MV) remains unknown. This study investigated whether AP could alleviate Dex-aggravated diaphragmatic dysfunction and explored its underlying mechanisms, focusing on autophagy. Female Sprague-Dawley rats were subjected to MV and treated with Dex, AP (Baihui and Yintang), and the autophagy inducer rapamycin (RAPA). Arterial blood gas parameters, vital signs, blood cell counts, and sedative dosage were recorded. Diaphragm function was evaluated by measuring contractile force, muscle fiber cross-sectional area, apoptosis, and oxidative stress markers, including superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), malondialdehyde (MDA), and angiotensin II (ANG II). Autophagy levels were assessed using the LC3-II/LC3-I ratio, p62 expression, and autophagosome accumulation. AP reduced the total Dex dosage by 54.7% (0.102 ± 0.005 mg vs. 0.225 ± 0.009 mg in the MV + Dex group, p < 0.001) while maintaining stable physiological parameters. MV decreased diaphragm contractility and myofiber cross-sectional area and increased MAFbx expression, apoptosis, and oxidative stress markers. Dex further worsened these parameters, whereas AP improved diaphragm function and attenuated atrophy, apoptosis, and oxidative stress. MV and MV + Dex groups exhibited excessive autophagy, as shown by autophagic vacuole accumulation, an increased LC3-II/LC3-I ratio, and decreased p62 expression. AP inhibited these autophagic changes, while RAPA partially reversed its protective effects. AP at Baihui and Yintang reduced Dex requirements and alleviated MV- and Dex-induced diaphragm dysfunction in rats by inhibiting excessive autophagy.

papers.title: A Placebo Acupuncture Device for Standardized Acupuncture Control Procedures.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Wu Y, Lin S, Zhang F, Xiao L, Li Y et al.
papers.abstract: Reliable placebo controls are difficult to implement in acupuncture trials because skin penetration, insertion direction, tactile feedback, and operator-participant interactions can reveal treatment allocation. This article describes a predefined-angle placebo acupuncture device designed to standardize a penetrating real-needle procedure and a nonpenetrating pressure-contact control while supporting allocation concealment for participants and treating acupuncturists. The system combines an opaque sleeve, matched 25 mm external needle exposure, a 0.35 mm x 65 mm sharp real needle or a 0.35 mm x 42 mm blunt placebo needle, internal resistance-generating material, and a medical-grade adhesive pad. In the present feasibility study, Yintang (DU29; historically also designated EX-HN3 in some international nomenclature systems) was treated using a predefined 30° oblique configuration, whereas right Hegu (LI4) was treated using a perpendicular configuration. At full advancement, the real needle penetrated approximately 25 mm, whereas the blunt placebo tip extended approximately 2 mm beyond the adhesive pad and compressed the skin without penetration. In 60 healthy volunteers randomized 1:1, no statistically significant between-group difference in VAS-rated needling discomfort was observed (4.63 ± 1.56 vs. 4.97 ± 1.67; t = -0.7976, p = 0.4283). Agreement between actual allocation and participant guesses was minimal (Cohen's κ = 0.033, 95% CI: -0.218 to 0.285), and agreement with acupuncturist guesses was low (κ = 0.133, 95% CI: -0.117 to 0.384). Group-specific Bang Blinding Index confidence intervals all included zero, although the relatively wide intervals did not exclude partial unblinding. These findings provide preliminary estimates of treatment-guessing behavior rather than confirmation of successful blinding. The placebo configuration should be regarded as a nonpenetrating pressure-contact control, not a physiologically inert placebo.
